title: Mouse brain regions farther from the retina in the Allen connectome had less reliable visual spike responses in 39 mice, but distance-preserving rewired connectomes predicted this equally well
abstract: Question: a prior SCI study found that the response reliability of mouse brain regions decreases with weighted connectome distance from the retina (D_ret). Does this rule generalize to new mice, stimuli and time scales, and does it need the specific wiring? Data: Allen OpenScope Barcoding (14 new mice; full-field flicker and flickering gratings) and Vision2Hippocampus (25 mice; moving bar), Neuropixels; Knox 2019 mesoscale connectome with Allen retinal tracer entry. Unit reliability is the odd-even repeat correlation after random thinning of spikes to an equal count. The plan was frozen before region values were computed. Results: region reliability decreased with D_ret in all four planned tests (Spearman rho -0.52 flicker, -0.43 gratings, -0.46 fine band below 25 ms, -0.43 bar; 41-44 regions; all mouse-bootstrap samples negative). It stayed after control of distance from LGd, firing rate and mouse, and inside the isocortex (rho -0.82 to -0.87). Region values agreed across data sets (rho 0.88). But the planned wiring-specificity test failed: 1,000 rewired connectomes that keep each target's input shares by source distance gave nearly the same correlations (mean rho -0.40 to -0.42; p 0.19-0.42). Exploratory: inside the isocortex the real wiring did better than the rewired graphs (p 0.002-0.013), and a simple hop count was the best predictor (rho -0.58 to -0.68). Limitations: an average-mouse connectome model; one null design; the result depends on the choice of retinal entry regions; visual stimuli only; exploratory results need independent confirmation.

display.caption: Region reliability (equal-count thinned split-half r) against weighted connectome distance from the retina, for four conditions. Point size grows with unit count; color shows the major brain division. Title gives Spearman rho with mouse-bootstrap 95% CI.

Observed rho (black line), mouse-bootstrap distribution with the real connectome (blue) and rho from 1,000 distance-preserving rewired connectomes (orange). The rewired graphs give nearly the same correlation.

Left: Spearman rho of six structural predictors with region reliability in four conditions (exploratory). Right: region reliability agrees between Barcoding flicker and Vision2Hippocampus bar data (30 shared regions).

citations.reason: We replicate its reliability-D_ret relation in new mice and stimuli and re-analyze its data set, but a distance-preserving rewired-connectome null predicts the relation equally well across the whole brain. We follow its D_ret definition and use its shared Vision2Hippocampus cache.
We use the shared Barcoding spike and unit cache that this study made.
